newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MIGHTY DORTMUND SHOW NO MERCY TO LITTLE AUXERRE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIGHTY DORTMUND SHOW NO MERCY TO LITTLE AUXERRE.

text.p: Auxerre found out they were just a brave little club as mighty Borussia Dortmund moved past them to reach the semifinals of the European Cup on Wednesday.
"We just have to admit that they are a better team than we are," said Auxerre trainer Guy Roux after his team lost the second leg of their quarter-final tie 1-0 in front of their home fans.
"They have stronger individuals and their organisation is superior to ours," added Roux, whose side were 3-1 down after the first leg in Germany.
Auxerre, a club from a small town in Burgundy with relatively limited means, dreamed of greatness after winning both the French league and Cup titles last year.
But they then lost the few stars they had as Laurent Blanc, Christophe Cocard and Corentin Martins all left the club.

Currently seventh in the league and not sure of playing in Europe next season, they were looking forward to becoming the fifth French club in as many years to advance to the last four of the European Cup after Marseille, Monaco, Paris St Germain and Nantes.
They were also seeking to avenge a defeat on penalties to Dortmund in a UEFA Cup semifinal tie in 1993.
But Borussia resisted first half pressure before carving out an opening in the 59th minute with a powerful long range shot by Lars Ricken for the only goal of the match.

"We had several opportunities while they only had two but they scored a goal," said Roux. "That says it all. We saw the huge difference between the seventh in the French league and the leader in the German league."
Dortmund, still top of the Bundesliga despite their clumsy 4-1 loss to Stuttgart on Saturday, now go on to face Manchester United for a place in the final.
They will be at home in the first leg on April 9, with the second leg at Old Trafford on April 23.

For the first leg, Borussia will be without defender and captain Matthias Sammer, who received his second yellow card in the competition on Wednesday for a nasty tackle on Bernard Diomede in the second half.
But key wing-back Stefan Reuter, who missed the match in Auxerre after being sent off in the first leg, will be back in action.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld sounded reasonably confident.

"We had come here to defend our lead, not to play exciting football", he said. "The most important thing was to defend, which we did well. Guys like Sammer, (Andreas) Moeller or Paulo Sousa have very rarely played together and they seem to get on well."
Hitzfeld warned United that Dortmund would probably improve from their showing against Auxerre. "We are not at 100 per cent yet but we're getting stronger," he said.
"I think that in the semifinals, we will be stronger than we were today (Wednesday).The next few weeks should bring us satisfactions."
Auxerre will meanwhile concentrate on fighting in the French league for a place in Europe next season.
"We have nine matches left and the lessons Dortmund taught us will probably be useful," Roux said.
